idiom_name: custom ILogger/ILoggerProvider with a chained HMACSHA256 authenticator
implementation_notes: Microsoft.Extensions.Logging already supplies the chokepoint: implement ILoggerProvider.CreateLogger and an ILogger whose Log<TState> canonicalises state, scopes and exception, chains an HMACSHA256 tag over the previous tag and appends to a write-only sink. Register the provider as a singleton so exactly one object owns the chain state, and put the sink behind an interface whose only write operation is append; the classic hand-written form is justified mainly when the audit stream must live outside the dependency-injection host (a tiny standalone writer owned by the process).
pitfalls: A provider registered as transient or scoped produces one chain state per resolution; register it as a singleton (AddSingleton<ILoggerProvider, ...>) or the sequence numbers fork.
Structured state and scopes can carry secrets through message templates or exception messages - redact in the provider, because the append-only store will keep whatever reaches it.

ILogger.Log is called concurrently from thread-pool threads; guard the chain state (lock, dedicated writer channel, or a single-consumer Channel<T>) instead of relying on the sink being internally synchronised.
